profiles.name: Hannah Braunstein
profiles.draft: Hannah Braunstein’s practice biography describes work with adults, adolescents and couples, with a focus on trauma, relationship difficulties, anxiety and depression. She describes an approach drawing on EMDR, Brainspotting and mindfulness. Her biography reports two master’s degrees from Washington University in St. Louis and undergraduate study in cultural anthropology at Cornell University.
profiles.sourceMap: All three sentences: official Meet Hannah biography.

profiles.name: Nancy Hyatt
profiles.draft: Nancy Hyatt describes her work as individual and couples psychotherapy focused on emotional patterns and relationships. Her website presents an approach influenced by Imago therapy, EMDR, Accelerated Resolution Therapy and body-focused practices. She also describes teaching within Mobius Executive Leadership and previous leadership roles with the Mid-Atlantic Imago and Relational Therapists Association.

profiles.name: Rachel Bradley Williams
profiles.draft: Rachel Bradley Williams’ practice biography describes work with children, adolescents, adults and families. She presents a strengths-based approach that considers clients’ relationships, developmental stages and mind-body connection. Her listed education includes an MSW from Howard University and a psychology degree from California State University, Northridge, followed by a two-year post-MSW clinical training fellowship at Yale University.
